full_text_en:
Shaanxi Xiyue Villa Co., Ltd. v. China Construction Third Engineering Bureau Jianfa Engineering Co., Ltd. and China Construction Third Engineering Bureau Third Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. — dispute over a construction project contract

Ruling Summary

According to the provisions of Article 79 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, a creditor may assign all or part of its contractual rights to a third party, except where such assignment is prohibited by the nature of the contract, by agreement of the parties, or by law or regulation. Laws and regulations do not prohibit the assignment of claims under a construction project contract. Where the parties to a construction project contract have not agreed that the claims under the contract may not be assigned, and the creditor assigns the claims to a third party and notifies the debtor, the assignment is legally valid and effective. The creditor is not required to obtain the debtor's consent for the assignment.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2007) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 10

Appellant (defendant at first instance and counterclaim plaintiff): Shaanxi Xiyue Villa Co., Ltd., domiciled at Kangfu Road, Huayin City, Shaanxi Province.
Legal Representative: Zhang Liyang, Chairperson of the Board of the company.
Agent ad litem: Xu Bangwei, lawyer at Beijing Jingtian & Gongcheng Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Dong Chungang, trainee lawyer at Beijing Jingtian & Gongcheng Law Firm.

Appellee (plaintiff at first instance and counterclaim defendant): China Construction Third Engineering Bureau Jianfa Engineering Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 552 Guanshan 1st Road, Hongshan District, Wuhan City, Hubei Province.
Legal Representative: Li Quanli, Chairperson of the Board of the company.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Xiaofei, lawyer at Shaanxi Renhewanguo Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Xiao Jian, lawyer at Beijing Zhongrui Law Firm.

Appellee (third party at first instance): China Construction Third Engineering Bureau Third Construction Engineering Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 552 Guanshan 1st Road, Hongshan District, Wuhan City, Hubei Province.
Legal Representative: Li Quanli, Chairperson of the Board of the company.
Agent ad litem: Chen Changkai, male, employee of the company.
Agent ad litem: Tian Lili, female, employee of the company.

The appellant Shaanxi Xiyue Villa Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xiyue Villa), dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2005) Shan Min Yi Chu Zi No. 10 rendered by the Shaanxi High People's Court in the case of dispute over a construction project contract with the appellees China Construction Third Engineering Bureau Jianfa Engineering Co., Ltd. (formerly Wuhan China Construction Third Engineering Bureau Jianfa Engineering Co., Ltd., hereinafter referred to as Jianfa Company) and China Construction Third Engineering Bureau Third Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. (formerly China Construction Third Engineering Bureau Third Construction and Installation Engineering Company, hereinafter referred to as the Third Company), appealed to this court. This court formed a collegial panel according to law and held a hearing of this case on February 12, 2007. The authorized agents of the appellant Xiyue Villa, Xu Bangwei and Dong Chungang, the authorized agents of the appellee Jianfa Company, Zhang Xiaofei and Xiao Jian, and the authorized agents of the appellee Third Company, Chen Changkai and Tian Lili, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found through trial: On November 30, 2001, Xiyue Villa (Party A) and the Third Company (Party B) entered into a Construction Project Construction Contract (hereinafter referred to as the Construction Contract) for the Huashan Holiday Hotel project owned by Xiyue Villa, stipulating that the commencement and completion dates of the project were from December 26, 2001 to October 31, 2002. Contract price: based on the final settlement price; the project was a turnkey contract (contractor providing both labor and materials), calculated in accordance with the 1999 "Shaanxi Province Comprehensive Budget Quota for Construction Projects," the "National Unified Installation Engineering Budget Quota Shaanxi Province Price List" (2001 edition), and the supporting "Shaanxi Province Fee Quota for Construction Projects, Installation Projects, Antique Garden Projects, and Decoration Projects" (1999 edition) and relevant provincial and municipal cost documents; the project was charged according to a Class II project, with a 20% downward adjustment for four fee rates. Reward and penalty for construction period: For each day earlier or later than the contract period, an equal reward or penalty of 0.1‰ of the total contracted project cost of Party B was applied. Payment of contract price and adjustment of contract price: Pile foundation construction: Party A shall pay Party B an advance payment of RMB 3,000,000; payment for this project shall be based on progress milestones: upon completion of foundation works, Party A shall pay Party B an interim payment of RMB 3,000,000; upon completion of main structure works, Party A shall pay Party B an additional advance payment for decoration works of RMB 5,000,000; upon completion of 50% of decoration works, Party A shall pay Party B an interim payment of RMB 13,000,000; before the project is completed and delivered to Party A, Party A shall pay Party B RMB 10,000,000; after the project passes acceptance inspection, Party A shall pay Party B RMB 8,000,000; after the final acceptance of the project, except for a 5% quality retention bond, the remaining project payment shall be paid by Party A to Party B in installments within two years; the 5% quality retention bond shall be refunded by Party A to Party B in a lump sum after the warranty period expires. Adjustment of contract price: After the contract price is agreed, neither party may change it without authorization, except in the following circumstances: increase or decrease in quantities confirmed by Party A's representative; design changes or project consultations confirmed by Party A's representative; price adjustments announced by the project cost management department; suspension of work due to water, electricity, or gas supply stoppages not caused by Party B for more than 8 hours cumulatively within one week, and resulting in economic losses; other additions or adjustments agreed in the contract; Party B shall notify Party A's representative in writing of the reasons and amount of adjustment within 10 days after the occurrence of the above circumstances; after approval by Party A's representative, the handling bank and Party B shall be notified; if Party A's representative does not respond within 10 days after receiving Party B's notice, it shall be deemed approved; if Party B fails to handle the matter promptly as required, causing project delays, Party B shall be responsible; if Party A fails to handle the review, signature, and payment promptly as required, Party B may send a payment request notice to Party A; if Party A still fails to pay as required within 5 days after receiving Party B's notice, Party A shall bear liability for breach of contract. Completion and settlement: If Party A's representative, within 10 days after receiving the completion acceptance report submitted by Party B, has no justifiable reason to organize the acceptance, or fails to approve within 5 days after the acceptance and cannot propose amendments, the completion acceptance shall be deemed approved, and settlement procedures may be conducted. If Party A, without justifiable reason, fails to carry out settlement within 30 days after approval of the completion report, starting from the 31st day, interest on the overdue project payment shall be paid at the interest rate of a construction enterprise borrowing from a bank for off-plan loans, and liability for breach of contract shall be borne. Liability for breach of contract: If Party A's representative fails to give necessary instructions, confirmations, or approvals in a timely manner, fails to perform its obligations or make payments in accordance with the contract, or commits other acts that prevent the performance of the contract, it shall bear liability for breach of contract (including paying the increased economic expenses incurred by Party B due to its breach and interest on the payable amounts calculated from the due date), and the construction period shall be extended accordingly; liquidated damages shall be paid in accordance with the terms of the agreement, and losses caused to Party B due to the breach, such as idle time, shall be compensated. If Party B fails to complete the project within the contract period, the construction quality fails to meet the design and specification requirements, or other acts occur that prevent the performance of the contract, Party A's representative may notify Party B, and Party B shall pay liquidated damages in accordance with the terms of the agreement and compensate for losses caused to Party A due to the breach. Unless the contract is terminated by agreement of both parties, or the contract cannot be performed due to one party's breach, the breaching party shall continue to perform the contract after bearing the above liability for breach; if the contract cannot be performed due to one party's breach, and the other party wishes to suspend or terminate the contract, it shall notify the breaching party 10 days in advance before suspending or terminating the contract, and the breaching party shall bear liability for breach. Meeting minutes, visa documents, various notices, letters of authorization, certificates, and other written materials arising during the performance of this contract shall be deemed supplemental terms to the contract and shall have the same effect as the contract terms. Additional terms: Materials required for this project shall be purchased and stored by Party B; steel and cement shall be purchased by Party B, with Party A providing financial guarantees; the price, quality, and quantity of any materials selected must be confirmed by Party A before purchase; overdue project payments shall not bear interest. On April 23, 2002, Xiyue Villa delivered the "Construction Project Commissioned Supervision Contract" signed with Shaanxi Linhua Engineering Supervision Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Supervision Company) to the Third Company and required it to accept supervision and management.

On July 30, 2002, the foundation works of Zones 1 and 2 passed inspection. On September 20, 2002, the "Meeting Minutes" signed by Xiyue Villa and the Third Company stipulated: After the plain soil backfill in Zone 1 and half of the plain soil backfill in Zone 2 of the Huashan Holiday Hotel, Xiyue Villa shall pay RMB 1,000,000 within one week; after the masonry team enters the site, Xiyue Villa shall pay RMB 500,000 within one week; the main materials for the later stage of the project shall be supplied or paid on behalf by Xiyue Villa; the main structure of Zone 1 shall be topped out by October 10, Zone 3 by October 15, plain soil backfill in Zone 1 shall be completed within 25 days, plain soil backfill in Zone 2 shall be completed by the 40th day, earth excavation in Zone 4 shall start on October 15, the staff dormitory construction shall start on September 25, and Xiyue Villa guarantees a one-time payment of no less than RMB 3,000,000 within one week; Zone 3 guarantees timely construction of the basement and timely backfill after completion, and after approval by Party A's General Manager Zhang, RMB 500,000 shall be paid. On March 11, 2003, the foundation works of Zone 3 passed inspection. On April 11, 2003, the main structure works passed inspection. On March 17, 2003, Xiyue Villa and the Installation Branch of China Construction Third Engineering Bureau Third Company signed a supplementary agreement for installation works. In July 2003, the Third Company obtained a Safe and Civilized Construction Site award plaque issued by the Weinan City Urban and Rural Construction Bureau.

On April 14, 2004, the Third Company sent a notice of assignment of claims to Xiyue Villa, stating: "Your company and our company entered into a construction project construction contract in 2002. Now, due to the needs of our company's restructuring and reorganization, we intend to assign the above claims that our company holds against your company to Wuhan China Construction Third Engineering Bureau Jianfa Industrial Development Company." Xiyue Villa signed and received it.

On September 29, 2004, Xiyue Villa and Jiangsu Huanjian Construction Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huanjian Company) signed a "Construction Project Construction Contract" (concerning water supply, drainage, strong and weak current, and HVAC works); on October 1, 2004, Xiyue Villa and Huayin Yongtai Construction Company signed a "Construction Project Construction Contract" (concerning the unfinished civil engineering works of the Huashan Holiday Hotel). On October 10, 2005, the Third Company sent a "Notice of Termination of Contract" to Xiyue Villa.

On January 19, 2006, upon the application of both parties, the court of first instance commissioned Shaanxi Sanqin Engineering Cost Consulting Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Sanqin Cost Company) to appraise the cost of the completed works by the Third Company involved in the case, the project payments already made by Xiyue Villa, and the amount of outstanding payments. On June 20, 2006, the appraisal conclusion made by Sanqin Cost Company was as follows: 1. Based on the structural construction drawings of the Huashan Holiday Hotel designed by China Light Industry Xi'an Design Institute, deducting the quantities not done and confirmed, plus on-site visas, the cost of civil engineering works completed by the Third Company for the Huashan Holiday Hotel (including staff dormitory) was calculated to be RMB 23,121,871.05 (excluding labor insurance coordination fees and safety and civilized construction site fees). 2. Based on the construction drawings designed by China Light Industry Xi'an Design Institute, on-site visas, and records of quantities completed by the Third Company provided by both parties, the cost of installation works completed by the Third Company for the Huashan Holiday Hotel (including staff dormitory) was calculated to be RMB 1,607,359.51 (excluding labor insurance coordination fees and safety and civilized construction site fees). 3. It was confirmed that Xiyue Villa had paid a total of RMB 15,199,163.76 in project payments and material payments. The appraisal report also detailed the disputed costs of works and disputed payment items. On June 27, 2006, the appraisal report was served on the three parties. The parties raised written objections to the appraisal report within the prescribed time limit. On July 26, 2006, the court of first instance conducted a court examination of the appraisal report, and Sanqin Cost Company appeared in court to accept questioning from the parties. After the hearing, Sanqin Cost Company provided a written response to the parties' inquiries. On August 2, 2006, the response was served on the three parties.

It was also found that: On December 27, 2002, China Construction Third Engineering Bureau Third Construction and Installation Engineering Company changed its registration to China Construction Third Engineering Bureau Third Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. On November 17, 2004, Wuhan China Construction Third Engineering Bureau Jianfa Engineering Co., Ltd. changed its registration to China Construction Third Engineering Bureau Jianfa Engineering Co., Ltd.

Between July 2002 and April 2003, the Third Company repeatedly urged Xiyue Villa for interim payments. On October 29, 2004, the Third Company sent a "Work Contact Sheet," "On-Site Change Visa Sheet," and "Letter to Shaanxi Xiyue Villa Co., Ltd. on the Issue of Progress Report Quantity for Huashan Holiday Hotel" by express mail to Xiyue Villa, requesting confirmation of extension of construction period, idle time costs, and machinery standstill costs. Xiyue Villa also provided a large number of supervision meeting minutes, work contact sheets, and other evidence to show that the Third Company's construction was non-standard, the project quality was unqualified, management was lax, and the project was delayed.

In July 2002, the Third Company signed a water supply agreement with Shaanxi Rongyu Junren Rehabilitation Hospital. On April 12, 2006, Shaanxi Rongyu Junren Rehabilitation Hospital issued a certificate stating that the Third Company owed a total of RMB 13,307.68 in water bills from June 24, 2003 to December 21, 2005, which had not been paid. The electricity bill of RMB 137,932.97 paid by Xiyue Villa for the construction site from August 2002 to May 2003 was undisputed by both parties (the appraisal report included it as a payment made by Xiyue Villa). The Third Company and Jianfa Company did not recognize the electricity bill of RMB 63,513.52 claimed by Xiyue Villa for the period from July 2003 to September 2004.

Jianfa Company believed that Xiyue Villa had violated the contract by defaulting on project payments and causing idle time losses, and therefore filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting: (1) a judgment ordering Xiyue Villa to pay the outstanding project payments and idle time losses totaling RMB 23,213,450 to Jianfa Company in accordance with the contract; (2) Xiyue Villa to bear all litigation costs, preservation fees, and attorney fees of this case; (3) Jianfa Company to have a priority right of compensation for the project it undertook.

Xiyue Villa filed a counterclaim, arguing that the Third Company had violated the contract by delivering the project late, causing economic losses to Xiyue Villa, and requested a judgment ordering Jianfa Company and the Third Company to: (1) pay liquidated damages of RMB 1,552,460 for the delay; (2) compensate Xiyue Villa for additional project payments of RMB 1,472,921; (3) compensate Xiyue Villa for business losses of RMB 8,558,237 due to the delay in delivery and use of the project; (4) bear all litigation costs of this case.

The court of first instance held that: The "Construction Contract" signed between Xiyue Villa and the Third Company represented the true intentions of both parties, did not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and should be a valid contract. The Third Company assigned its contractual claims to Jianfa Company and served a notice of assignment of claims on Xiyue Villa, which was in compliance with relevant laws and regulations. The assignment was the true intention of the assignor and assignee, did not harm the interests of the debtor, and was legally valid. Jianfa Company therefore acquired the contractual claims that the Third Company should have enjoyed. Since the Huashan Holiday Hotel project was still under construction, and Xiyue Villa and the Third Company had not yet made a final settlement of the project payment, the amount of contractual claims enjoyed by Jianfa Company had not been determined; the amounts of project payments already made by Xiyue Villa were also disputed between the Third Company and Xiyue Villa. Upon the application of both parties, the court of first instance commissioned Sanqin Cost Company to appraise the cost of the project and the payments made by Xiyue Villa. The appraisal conclusion had been examined in court by the parties and should be confirmed by law.

Regarding the cost of disputed works listed separately in the appraisal report, after review by the court of first instance, the following determinations should be made: 1. Concerning the disputed works cost, for the quantities reported by the Third Company but not recognized by Xiyue Villa, based solely on the quantities reported by the Third Company, without the visas of Xiyue Villa and the supervision company, the quantities could not be confirmed. The civil engineering and installation costs involved in that portion were not confirmed. 2. Concerning whether the safety and civilized construction site fee should be charged. The safety and civilized construction site fee for civil engineering cost was calculated to be RMB 221,299.07, and for installation cost to be RMB 15,504.62. Since the construction site had been awarded the Safe and Civilized Construction Site by the Weinan Urban and Rural Construction Bureau, this fee should be charged according to regulations and adjusted with the project cost. 3. Concerning the disputed payments made. The disputed water bill from June 24, 2003 to December 21, 2005 was RMB 13,307.68 (of which RMB 4,003.96 from June 24 to August 21, 2003; RMB 1,692.60 from September 21 to November 24, 2003; and RMB 7,611.12 from November 24, 2003 to December 21, 2005). Since the invoices could not be clearly distinguished, and because Xiyue Villa had signed a construction contract with Huanjian Company on September 29, 2004, it was determined that for the water bill of RMB 13,307.68, the amount of RMB 5,696.56 incurred before November 24, 2003 should be borne by the Third Company, and the amount of RMB 7,611.12 incurred from November 24, 2003 to December 21, 2005 should be borne equally by Xiyue Villa and the Third Company. The expenses for materials such as stone chips, sand, distribution boxes, conduits, and fittings purchased by Xiyue Villa totaling RMB 407,078.71, since there was no material receipt from the Third Company, this amount was not included in the project cost and should not be included in the payments made. The loan of RMB 10,000 by Hou Hongwei belonged to a different legal relationship and was not involved in this case. The charge of RMB 20,000 collected by the Labor Service Company of the Power Supply Bureau was for line maintenance and should not be included in the payments made. The electricity bill of RMB 63,513.52 paid by Xiyue Villa on behalf of the Third Company from July 2003 to September 2004 should be borne by the Third Company and deducted from the project payment to be settled. In summary, although there was dispute, the total amount to be included in payments made was RMB 73,015.64.

In summary, Xiyue Mountain Villa shall pay a total project cost of RMB 24,992,875.13. After deducting the project costs, material costs, and water and electricity fees already paid by Xiyue Mountain Villa on behalf of the other party, totaling RMB 15,273,309.40, Xiyue Mountain Villa shall pay Jianfa Company the remaining project cost of RMB 9,719,565.73. Pursuant to Article 286 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Jianfa Company has a priority right to be compensated from the project cost payable by Xiyue Mountain Villa within the scope of the project. Since the Huashan Holiday Hotel project has not yet been completed, both parties bear some responsibility. The delay in the project schedule was jointly caused by Xiyue Mountain Villa's failure to make full payment, and by San Company's nonstandard construction, lax construction management, and rework. Accordingly, the first instance court did not support Jianfa Company's claim for losses from work stoppage or Xiyue Mountain Villa's counterclaim for a penalty for delay in the project period. Regarding Xiyue Mountain Villa's claim for additional expenses, because the costs related to the construction by Huanjian Company and other entities were not included in the construction cost appraisal in this case, Xiyue Mountain Villa did not incur additional expenses, and the first instance court also did not support this claim. Regarding Xiyue Mountain Villa's claim for losses from delayed operation, because the evidence it provided could not prove the amount of losses from the delayed opening, and San Company could not have foreseen the management contracts with IHG and other companies, the court lawfully refused to admit this evidence and did not support the claim. The first instance court, in accordance with Articles 7, 8, 60, 80, and 286 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, ruled as follows: (1) Within thirty days from the effective date of this judgment, Xiyue Mountain Villa shall pay Jianfa Company the project cost of RMB 9,719,565.73; (2) Jianfa Company has a priority right to be compensated from the project cost owed by Xiyue Mountain Villa for the project; (3) All other claims of Jianfa Company are dismissed; (4) The counterclaim of Xiyue Mountain Villa is dismissed. The first instance case acceptance fee was RMB 126,077.25, the appraisal fee was RMB 165,000, totaling RMB 291,077.25, of which Jianfa Company shall bear RMB 174,646.35 and Xiyue Mountain Villa shall bear RMB 116,430.90; the counterclaim fee was RMB 67,928.08, to be borne by Xiyue Mountain Villa; the litigation preservation fee was RMB 109,738, to be borne by Jianfa Company.

Xiyue Mountain Villa, dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, appealed to this Court, arguing that the first instance judgment erred in both fact-finding and application of law. (1) The first instance judgment ruled that the assignment of the contractual claims by San Company to Jianfa Company was valid. Based on the nature of the contract, the contractual claims in this case were not assignable by law. At the time of assignment, the conditions for settlement of the project were completely absent. The creditor-debtor relationship between San Company and Xiyue Mountain Villa could not be determined. Xiyue Mountain Villa only noted receipt of the notice on the receipt and did not consent to the assignment. (2) Xiyue Mountain Villa had overpaid the project cost and did not fail to make payments. (3) San Company admitted that during construction, it failed to start work according to the construction schedule, had work stoppages, substandard construction quality, and unqualified construction practices. San Company should pay liquidated damages to Xiyue Mountain Villa as agreed. By failing to complete the main structure and gradually withdrawing from the site after February 2004, San Company caused the contract to be impossible to perform. Due to San Company's deliberate breach, the Huashan Holiday Hotel could not be completed on time, and San Company should bear the losses from the delayed completion. Xiyue Mountain Villa's counterclaim should be supported by law. (4) The first instance judgment included taxes corresponding to civil and installation works, fees for safe and civilized construction sites, and civilized construction subsidies in the project cost as per the appraisal, which exceeded the contract terms. The contract terms should prevail. (5) San Company unilaterally proposed to terminate the contract, but Xiyue Mountain Villa did not agree. The Construction Contract should still be performed. (6) Jianfa Company, being a third party not a party to the Construction Contract, was neither the contracted constructor nor the contractor of the construction project. Therefore, Jianfa Company's exercise of a priority right over the project lacked legal basis. In view of this, Xiyue Mountain Villa requested: (1) to set aside the first instance judgment and dismiss all claims of the appellee; (2) to support all counterclaims of the appellant; (3) to order the appellee to bear all litigation costs.

The appellees, Jianfa Company and San Company, argued: (1) Regarding the assignment of claims. San Company and Jianfa Company reached an agreement on the assignment of claims in this case and notified the debtor of the agreement. The assignment was lawful and valid. (2) Regarding the arrears of project costs. Xiyue Mountain Villa did not pay the project costs in accordance with the contract. As of April 14, 2003, there were as many as 16 written confirmations and minutes of supervision meetings demanding payment, proving that Xiyue Mountain Villa had seriously fallen behind in payments. On October 29, 2004, San Company sent a payment demand to Xiyue Mountain Villa by notarized delivery, but Xiyue Mountain Villa refused to perform its payment obligation. Its conduct constituted a fundamental breach, and San Company had the right to suspend performance. San Company's failure to complete the project on time did not constitute a breach. (3) Regarding the termination of the Construction Contract. Xiyue Mountain Villa's breach, especially the illegal re-letting of the project, made it impossible to achieve the purpose of the contract, and San Company lawfully obtained the right to terminate the contract. (4) Regarding Xiyue Mountain Villa's claim for additional project payments. The work completed by Huanjian Company was not involved in this case. The project costs paid by Xiyue Mountain Villa for the construction did not constitute additional expenses. (5) Regarding Xiyue Mountain Villa's claim for loss of expected revenue. The profit and loss statement of IHG lacked the basic elements of evidence. San Company did not commit any breach and should not bear liability for breach.

After the second instance hearing, Xiyue Mountain Villa submitted to this Court evidence such as a certificate from San Company stating that it would not charge Xiyue Mountain Villa for declaring a civilized construction site. This Court holds that Xiyue Mountain Villa should have submitted this evidence within the time limit for evidence submission in the first instance. Its submission after the second instance hearing exceeded the time limit, and it did not explain the reason for the delay. According to Article 34 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, if a party fails to submit evidence within the time limit, it is deemed to have waived its right to present evidence. The evidence submitted by Xiyue Mountain Villa in the second instance has no probative force in this case.

The following facts were found in the second instance: Xiyue Mountain Villa was approved for establishment by the administrative department for industry and commerce on April 10, 2001, and obtained a business license as a legal person. On March 7, 2002, Xiyue Mountain Villa obtained the 2002-3 Construction Land Planning Permit and Construction Engineering Planning Permit issued by the urban planning department of the People's Government of Huayin City. The next day, it obtained the 2002-24 Construction Engineering Construction Permit issued by the Construction Bureau of Huayin City, which stated that the project name was Huashan Holiday Hotel, with a construction area of 43,000 square meters, a project cost of RMB 60 million, and a start date of March 8, 2002. In May 2003, Xiyue Mountain Villa obtained the State-Owned Land Use Certificates with numbers Yinguoyong (2003) Zi 606 and 607 issued by the People's Government of Huayin City.

The Construction Contract also stipulated that upon completion of the third floor of the main structure, Xiyue Mountain Villa would pay San Company an additional RMB 3 million in project costs; upon topping out of the main structure, Xiyue Mountain Villa would pay San Company an additional RMB 3 million in project costs. On March 19, 2002, Xiyue Mountain Villa had not yet provided San Company with construction drawings and geological survey data, nor had it resolved the water supply and power supply issues required for construction. When San Company excavated the foundation, it encountered large rocks and arranged for a rock crusher to break them. On April 15, 2002, San Company submitted the Construction Organization Design prepared based on the construction drawings to the supervision department. On June 5 of that year, the project supervisor issued review comments on the Construction Organization Design. On June 13 of that year, the main structure entered the second-floor roof slab construction, but Xiyue Mountain Villa had not yet provided installation drawings for the third floor and above.

Jianfa Company and San Company were both approved for establishment and obtained business licenses as legal persons on December 27, 2002. Jianfa Company's business scope includes general contracting, construction, and consulting for various types of construction projects. San Company's business scope includes general contracting of building decoration and renovation projects, steel structure projects, and housing construction projects.

Other facts in this case found in the second instance are the same as those found in the first instance judgment. On September 27, 2007, Jianfa Company stated to this Court that, on the condition that the original judgment was upheld in the second instance, it would waive RMB 200,000 of the civilized construction site quota fee during the enforcement stage and deduct it when applying for enforcement.

This Court holds that the Construction Contract signed between Xiyue Mountain Villa and San Company and the Meeting Minutes signed on September 20, 2002, represent the true intentions of both parties. The content of the contract and the minutes does not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and regulations and should be deemed lawful and valid. Both parties have obligations to perform. The delay in the project schedule was caused by the joint breach of contract by both Xiyue Mountain Villa and San Company, and both should bear liability for breach. This case involves the following key issues: (1) whether the assignment of claims by San Company to Jianfa Company is lawful and valid; (2) whether Xiyue Mountain Villa paid the full project cost to San Company in accordance with the project progress; (3) whether the Construction Contract should be terminated; (4) whether the items and amounts of project costs determined in the first instance are reasonable; (5) whether Xiyue Mountain Villa's counterclaim is established; (6) whether Jianfa Company enjoys a priority right to be compensated for the project it completed. These are discussed as follows:

1. Regarding whether the assignment of claims by San Company to Jianfa Company is lawful and valid.

In this case, San Company performed part of its contractual obligations and obtained the right to demand payment of corresponding project costs from Xiyue Mountain Villa. At the time of the assignment, San Company's claim had already arisen, and the amount of the claim was later confirmed by the appraisal conclusion in this case. After receiving the Notice of Assignment of Claims from San Company, Xiyue Mountain Villa did not raise any objection. Laws and regulations do not prohibit the assignment of claims under construction project construction contracts, and the assignment of claims does not require the consent of the debtor. Pursuant to Articles 80 and 81 of the Contract Law, this Court confirms that the assignment of claims in this case is lawful and valid. Jianfa Company therefore acquired San Company's claims against Xiyue Mountain Villa and the ancillary rights. Although Xiyue Mountain Villa argued that the claims in this case were not assignable by law, it did not provide any legal basis. Therefore, this Court does not support Xiyue Mountain Villa's contention that San Company's assignment of claims was invalid. Jianfa Company, based on its acquisition of San Company's claims, obtained the standing to sue in this case.

2. Regarding whether Xiyue Mountain Villa paid the full project cost to San Company in accordance with the project progress.

According to the terms of the Construction Contract, payment for the project was to be made according to the physical progress of the project. The payment here refers to Xiyue Mountain Villa's direct payment of project costs to San Company, and does not include the deduction of other expenses paid by Xiyue Mountain Villa for the project from the project costs. According to the project progress, on April 11, 2003, the main part of the Huashan Holiday Hotel passed inspection and acceptance, and San Company had also completed floor leveling and partial interior plastering. According to the progress, Xiyue Mountain Villa should have paid RMB 17 million in project costs. However, the project appraisal report confirmed that the total of project costs and material costs paid by Xiyue Mountain Villa was RMB 15,273,309.40. Xiyue Mountain Villa's failure to pay the project costs constituted a breach of contract and should bear corresponding liability for the delayed delivery of the project. Xiyue Mountain Villa's claim of overpaying project costs to San Company lacks factual basis, and this Court does not support it. Jianfa Company's claim that Xiyue Mountain Villa was in arrears with project costs is well-founded, and this Court supports it.

3. Regarding whether the Construction Contract should be terminated.

According to Article 18, Section 18-1 of the Construction Contract, if either party's breach makes it impossible to continue the performance of the contract, the other party may terminate the contract and shall notify the other party 10 days in advance, without requiring the other party's consent. Before San Company terminated the contract, it had already withdrawn from the construction site. Xiyue Mountain Villa then signed a new construction contract with Huanjian Company to continue the project. Objectively, the Construction Contract could no longer be performed. San Company's exercise of its right to terminate the contract was in accordance with the contract terms. This Court does not support Xiyue Mountain Villa's contention that San Company had no right to unilaterally terminate the contract without its consent. San Company shall settle the project costs based on the actual work completed.

4. Regarding whether the items and amounts of project costs determined in the first instance are reasonable.

In the first instance, the appraisal department responded to the objections raised by both parties regarding the appraisal conclusion of the project cost and adjusted the items for which the objections were reasonable. This Court holds that the first instance judgment already deducted the RMB 1,130 paid by Xiyue Mountain Villa for rock crushing labor costs from the project costs payable, and it is also reasonable not to adjust the cost of other project items raised by Xiyue Mountain Villa. Regarding whether taxes corresponding to civil and installation works, fees for safe and civilized construction sites, and civilized construction subsidies should be included in the project cost. According to Article 4 of the Construction Contract, the contract price was calculated based on the relevant quota for construction projects in Shaanxi Province in 1999. This quota includes taxes and fees for safety and civilized construction quotas. Therefore, the first instance judgment's inclusion of these two items in the project cost was in accordance with the contract and did not involve any additional charging items. This Court does not support Xiyue Mountain Villa's contention that the corresponding taxes, fees for safe and civilized construction sites, and civilized construction subsidies should not be included in the project cost.

5. Regarding whether Xiyue Mountain Villa's counterclaim is established.

First, regarding the claim for a penalty for delaying the project period. The reasons for the delayed delivery of the project were: first, Xiyue Mountain Villa delayed in going through the project approval procedures, obtaining the construction start permit more than four months later than the contractually agreed start date, and obtaining the State-Owned Land Use Certificate later than the contractually agreed completion date. Second, Xiyue Mountain Villa delayed in providing the construction drawings and failed to resolve the water and power supply required for construction before the start of construction. Construction according to drawings is an objective requirement for construction projects, but as of March 19, 2002, Xiyue Mountain Villa had not yet delivered the construction drawings to San Company, and the water and power supply were insufficient, preventing San Company from normal construction. Third, Xiyue Mountain Villa did not pay the project costs in full according to the progress, seriously affecting construction. San Company also had issues such as insufficient personnel and equipment on site, lax construction management, and rework, which affected the construction progress. In light of this, the first instance's finding that Xiyue Mountain Villa and San Company jointly caused the delay was not improper. Since Xiyue Mountain Villa had serious breaches, this Court does not support its contention that San Company should bear liability for damages. Second, regarding Xiyue Mountain Villa's claim for compensation for additional project costs paid. The project costs that the first instance judgment ordered Xiyue Mountain Villa to pay to Jianfa Company only included the project costs payable for the work completed by San Company. Xiyue Mountain Villa did not incur any additional expenses. Xiyue Mountain Villa's claim that Jianfa Company should compensate it for project costs under another contract lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it. Third, regarding Xiyue Mountain Villa's claim for losses from delayed operation. Since Xiyue Mountain Villa first breached the contract and failed to provide sufficient evidence to prove the amount of losses, this Court does not support this claim of Xiyue Mountain Villa.

6. Regarding whether Jianfa Company enjoys a priority right to be compensated for the project.

Project costs have a priority right nature. Jianfa Company acquired this right based on the assignment of claims. Given that the construction project has not yet been fully completed, and the Construction Contract was delayed due to Xiyue Mountain Villa's arrears in project costs and other reasons, the period for Jianfa Company to exercise its priority right should commence from the date the contract was terminated on October 10, 2005. Jianfa Company had already filed a lawsuit before that date, so it should not be determined that the period for exercising the priority right had exceeded six months. This Court does not support Xiyue Mountain Villa's contention that Jianfa Company had exceeded the period for exercising its priority right.

In conclusion, the assignment of claims by San Company to Jianfa Company is lawful and valid, and Jianfa Company has standing to sue. Both Xiyue Mountain Villa and San Company had breaches in the performance of the Construction Contract and both bear responsibility for the delay in project completion. However, since Xiyue Mountain Villa breached first and was in long-term arrears with project costs, and there were no additional expenses, the first instance court correctly dismissed Xiyue Mountain Villa's counterclaim. Given that the Construction Contract is indeed impossible to perform, San Company has the right to terminate the contract as agreed. After termination, the unperformed parts shall no longer be performed. Since the warranty period for the project as stipulated in the Construction Contract has expired, the warranty deposit shall no longer be deducted from the project costs. Based on the assignment of claims, Jianfa Company filed a lawsuit before the contract was terminated and enjoys a priority right to be compensated for the project. The first instance judgment found the facts to be basically clear and applied the law correctly. In the second instance, Jianfa Company proposed to waive RMB 200,000 of the civilized construction site quota fee during the enforcement stage and deduct it when applying for enforcement, which should be allowed by law. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

Failure to perform the monetary payment obligation under this judgment within the time limit shall result in double the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance, in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 126,077.25 shall be borne by Shaanxi Xiyue Mountain Villa Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
